kspl.serverPath.description:
Path to the Kanso LSP server executable.
If empty, the bundled server is used.
Machine-scoped on purpose: a workspace must not be able to point this at another program, because VS Code launches it when the folder is opened.

kspl.trace.server.description: Traces the communication between VS Code and the Kanso LSP server.

kspl.defines.description:
#cfg() flags to assume while analyzing, same as the compiler's -D (e.g. ["tls", "db"]).
Declarations guarded by a flag you do not list are dropped before analysis, exactly as the compiler drops them, so hover and go-to-definition return nothing there.

languages.$comment: Caution: **Do not give it the same id as kspl.** The two notations are told apart by the id alone — extension.js sends both to the language server (KSPL_LANGS), and ksplc reads each in the notation its name says. Rolled into one id, a document would be sent under the other notation's name and a syntax error would line up on every line. configuration points at the same file (the brackets, the auto-closing and the note notation are identical).
